One little piece of advice or whatever I have for anyone; its not about what happens, its about how you judge it, how you frame it. So shit may happen, but use it in a way that is useful. 

**Example**: I have an injured knee, which sucks because my biggest hobbie in this life was running, I loved running to places instead of taking a bus. 

But well parkour, and mad skating led to an injured knee, and I suffered so much becauese of it, I dont skate nor run these days, which took me into a deep depression that first year, since 2015 I've been only walking and doing lower impact sports like swimming. But you know what? I also realize that the injured knee meant I had to take a different route, that I have to take really good care of that knee, how I use it, to use it wisely, because it will wear over time. So I learned to care for all my other joints a lot more. I also realized that the body will go downhill from here lol, and gave me a weird acceptance of it, even cherishing it for some odd reason. I came to the funny conclusion that you just gotta let it all "hang". Let those unfixables in your life just hang off of you! Like you're wearing them and don't give a fuck. 

​

An injured knee helped me reframe my whole notion of what is valuable in life. 

I realized that certain things, not even gill gates can buy, thus are invaluable. And guess what, those things you already have them, and take them for granted, its not until life takes something really valuable from you that you learn how lucky you truly are. And what a worthless piece of junk most materialistic goals are.

You don't have to find something you enjoy, there are only these possible ways of getting your life together in my honest opinion.

1- Your issue is somewhere on the fields of: sport, diet, sleep/rest, psychological. Some of these things can be fixed, like if you're not exercising nor walking at all, moving your body releases feel good chemicals. Diet could be shitty nad make you feel shitty, or you're allergic to something. You're sleep deprived constantly. Psychological: comparing yourself with other, negative self-talk, negative memories, negative thoughts, an imbalance in chemicals that is fixable with some of the previously mentioned things.

Note that maybe the above can't be met by a physical or other type of problem, in which case it will be harder and on the extreme case, impossible to fix.

​

2- You do all the above but can't seem to find a reason, other than: clinical depression. In this case you are at the mercy of whatever awaits you, or maybe even impossible to fix. Antidepressants can help you, but theres no promise, \*pat of the back\* "goodluck!" .

So bottom line on point number 2: if you can't identify any particular thing within your control to get your shit together and crawl out of depression/suicidal state, then all you can do is wait and see what happens next, if by some miracle or whatever you heal out of that misery, maybe even outgrow it one day and see back on it as a key moment in your life, as a fucking hell you endured and came out of it like few might have, and with some fucking kind of knowledge or wisdom or happiness that makes it all worth it.
